mcu_g_0160_200000ec.name: motor_energy_window_rate
mcu_g_0160_200000ec.description: Windowed rate value of the energy budget limiter (mcu_0160_08003c78), in Q15 units. The limiter recomputes it every DAT_200000D8/20 calls from its integrated excess-power term (per the function note). mcu_0160_0800a320 reads it clamped to -0x7F333..+0x7F333. Telemetry frame 0x211 sends the value shifted right by 15 as one byte. Written only by the limiter in this packet; no reset here, so it presumably starts from zero at power-up.

mcu_g_0160_2000030c.name: protocol_telem_tick_count
mcu_g_0160_2000030c.description: Tick counter of the telemetry and CAN transmit schedule, incremented once per call of mcu_0160_0800dc08. Every 10th count it queues frames 0x211, 0x212 and 0x343, every 20th frames 0x341, 0x342 and 0x344, and every 50th frame 0x401. It is frozen while the start-up hold (DAT_20000320 bit 1, countdown DAT_20000322) runs and is zeroed when the hold ends. Not wrapped specially; the modulo tests assume it keeps counting.

mcu_g_0160_20000318.name: protocol_can_reinit_count
mcu_g_0160_20000318.description: Number of CAN1 recovery re-initialisations. mcu_0160_0800dc08 increments it (saturating at 0xFFFF) when its re-init sequence runs: CAN1 is reset and reconfigured, and its filters are rewritten. The sequence is started by flag DAT_2000031f after a delay of about 51 calls. Only the low byte goes into telemetry frame 0x341 (through the 0x312 field).

mcu_g_0160_20000338.name: protocol_uptime_coarse_count
mcu_g_0160_20000338.description: Start-up progress counter. mcu_0160_08007df4 increments it once per 10 calls while its own call counter DAT_200003b8 is below 100, so it reaches 10 after the first 100 calls and then stays there. It is sent as the first data byte of telemetry frame 0x344. Present in builds 143, 152 and 0160 only.

mcu_g_0160_2000033a.name: protocol_uptime_tick_count
mcu_g_0160_2000033a.description: Byte counter incremented on every call of mcu_0160_08007df4 after its first 100 calls, so it wraps at 256 (uptime-like, probably one count per scheduler tick). It is sent as the second data byte of telemetry frame 0x344, next to protocol_uptime_coarse_count. Present in builds 143, 152 and 0160 only.

mcu_g_0160_2000040c.name: protocol_telem_aux_byte
mcu_g_0160_2000040c.description: Single byte whose meaning is not known from this packet. Its only access here is the copy into telemetry frame 0x401 (mcu_telemetry_group_get). The writer is outside this packet. It is probably a status or identification byte, but this is a guess.

mcu_g_0160_200006b8.name: protocol_fwup_busy
mcu_g_0160_200006b8.description: Reentrancy guard of the firmware-transfer frame handler mcu_0160_0800672c. It is set to 1 on entry and cleared on exit. A frame that arrives while it is set gets an error reply with status 6 and clears the guard. The reset routine mcu_state_reset_load_key16 also clears it.

mcu_g_0160_200006b9.name: protocol_fwup_next_seq
mcu_g_0160_200006b9.description: Expected sequence byte of the next data frame in the firmware transfer. The reset sets it to 0, and each accepted data frame (command 8) increments it. A frame whose sequence byte equals the previous one is a retransmission and is answered without processing. Any other mismatch is rejected with status 5.

mcu_g_0160_200006ba.name: protocol_fwup_vector_ok
mcu_g_0160_200006ba.description: Set to 1 when the first data frame of the transfer (offset 0) passes the image sanity check. That check requires the first 32-bit word of the image to match the mask 0x2FFE0000 == 0x20000000, which is the form of a RAM stack-pointer value in a Cortex-M vector table. While this flag is 0, data frames are refused with status 7. The reset clears it.

mcu_g_0160_200006bb.name: protocol_fwup_checksum_ok
mcu_g_0160_200006bb.description: Set to 1 when the last word of the image matches the running checksum (see protocol_fwup_checksum_acc). The commit (command 9) requires it together with protocol_fwup_last_block_seen. Command 10 also tests it, with DAT_2000204c. The reset clears it.

mcu_g_0160_200006bc.name: protocol_fwup_last_block_seen
mcu_g_0160_200006bc.description: Set to 1 when a data frame reaches the last word of the image length from the start command. The final checksum comparison runs at that point. Once it is set, later data frames are accepted without writing flash, and the commit (command 9) requires it. The reset clears it.

mcu_g_0160_200006bd.name: protocol_fwup_frame_ok
mcu_g_0160_200006bd.description: Set to 1 after each data frame passes the initial checks in the data path, regardless of the later checksum result. The reset clears it. No read of this flag is in this packet, so it is probably a status for other code or for debugging.

mcu_g_0160_200006be.name: protocol_fwup_spare_flags
mcu_g_0160_200006be.description: Three bytes at 0x200006BE to 0x200006C0 that exist only in build 0160. The reset routine clears them, and nothing else in this packet reads or writes them. Their purpose is unknown; they sit between the transfer flags and the image length.

mcu_g_0160_200006c4.name: protocol_fwup_image_len
mcu_g_0160_200006c4.description: Length in bytes of the firmware image announced by the start command (command 7). The start command accepts only lengths from 1 to 0xE800 that are multiples of 8. Data frames must end within this length plus 0x80. The commit (command 9) copies it to 0x20002050. Flash staging begins at 0x08010800, so the largest image ends below the 0x0801F000 page.

mcu_g_0160_200006c8.name: protocol_fwup_bytes_received
mcu_g_0160_200006c8.description: Byte offset of the next image word in the firmware transfer. The start command sets it to 0, and it advances by 4 for each word of accepted data. Flash is written at 0x08010800 plus this value. When it equals 0x400, the frame runs a header comparison against RAM copies and flash constants before its write. Each time it reaches a multiple of 0x400, the key in protocol_fwup_xtea_key_word0 is stepped.

mcu_g_0160_200006cc.name: protocol_fwup_checksum_acc
mcu_g_0160_200006cc.description: Running 32-bit checksum of the decrypted image words. Each word before the last is added to it. The last word must equal the bit complement of the halfword-swapped sum, ~((acc << 16) | (acc >> 16)); the handler then stores that complemented value here. The reset clears it.

mcu_g_0160_200006d0.name: protocol_fwup_block_count
mcu_g_0160_200006d0.description: Number of 8-byte blocks in the announced image, which is the image length divided by 8. The start command sets it, and only the reset clears it. No other access is in this packet.

mcu_g_0160_200006d4.name: protocol_fwup_prev_block
mcu_g_0160_200006d4.description: The previous raw 8-byte block of firmware data. It is copied from protocol_fwup_cur_block before each new block is decrypted, and its bytes are XORed into the decrypted block (CBC-style chaining). The first block of the image is not XORed. The reset clears it.

mcu_g_0160_200006dc.name: protocol_fwup_cur_block
mcu_g_0160_200006dc.description: The most recent raw (still encrypted) 8-byte block taken from a data frame. It is loaded before the block is decrypted in place by mcu_xtea_decrypt_with_key, and at the next block it is shifted into protocol_fwup_prev_block. The reset clears it.

mcu_g_0160_20000b80.name: protocol_drive_enable_flag
mcu_g_0160_20000b80.description: One-byte flag that gates the drive. It is probably 1 for enabled and 0 for disabled, though the writer is not in this packet. When it is 0, mcu_0160_08004e78 forces the state byte at DAT_200000f8 + 0x239 to 1 and clears DAT_20000898. It is also copied to DAT_200000f8 + 0x2e4 and carried in telemetry frame 0x343.

mcu_g_0160_20001860.name: protocol_msg2_rec_flags
mcu_g_0160_20001860.description: Byte of the ring-2 CAN record under construction. mcu_msg_ring2_enqueue_frames writes it as 0 for every record it stores, so it is probably a flags or sub-index field that is always 0 here. The record is: this byte, an unused byte at 0x20001861, the length byte at 0x20001862, and 8 data bytes at 0x20001863. The CAN ID word is at 0x20001858, outside this packet.

mcu_g_0160_20001862.name: protocol_msg2_rec_len
mcu_g_0160_20001862.description: Number of valid payload bytes (0 to 8) in the ring-2 record being built by mcu_msg_ring2_enqueue_frames. A longer payload is split into records of at most 8 bytes, and the length is set for each record before it is stored. It is 0 when the payload is empty.

mcu_g_0160_20001863.name: protocol_msg2_rec_data
mcu_g_0160_20001863.description: The 8-byte payload of the ring-2 record. mcu_msg_ring2_enqueue_frames copies up to 8 bytes of the caller's buffer here with the memcpy routine, and the record is then passed to the next stage, FUN_08008ce4 (not described here). Only the first protocol_msg2_rec_len bytes are valid.

mcu_g_0160_20001ff0.name: protocol_telem_word_1ff0
mcu_g_0160_20001ff0.description: 16-bit value returned by mcu_0160_0800ce80 (not described in this packet). mcu_0160_0800e238 refreshes it on every call of the control-loop status update. Telemetry frames 0x210 and 0x212 carry it as payload bytes 2 and 3.

mcu_g_0160_20001ff4.name: protocol_telem_temp_a
mcu_g_0160_20001ff4.description: Byte that telemetry frames 0x211 and 0x212 send. mcu_0160_0800e238 sets it to DAT_20000026 + 20, saturated to 0..255 and probably a temperature in degrees C with a 20-degree offset. If DAT_20000a7c is nonzero, that value is used instead. The source of DAT_20000a7c is not named in this packet.

mcu_g_0160_20001ff5.name: protocol_telem_temp_b
mcu_g_0160_20001ff5.description: Byte that telemetry frame 0x401 sends. mcu_0160_0800e238 sets it from DAT_20000024 + 20, saturated to 0..255 and probably a temperature in degrees C with a 20-degree offset. If DAT_20000b18 is nonzero, that value is used instead. Same pattern as protocol_telem_temp_a, for the other sensor.

mcu_g_0160_20001ff6.name: protocol_telem_count_1ff6
mcu_g_0160_20001ff6.description: Copy of the byte DAT_200003bc, made by mcu_0160_0800e238 on each control-loop status update. The start-up code zeroes it. Telemetry frames 0x210 and 0x212 send it as payload byte 6. Its source is not named in this packet, so its exact meaning is unknown.

mcu_g_0160_20002044.name: protocol_telem_scaled_centi
mcu_g_0160_20002044.description: Signed 32-bit value computed in mcu_0160_0800a320 from DAT_20000a48, scaled by a fixed-point factor. Telemetry frame 0x401 sends it divided by 100 as one byte, so the unit is probably 0.01 of a physical quantity such as volts or amps. The exact physical quantity is not named in this packet.

mcu_g_0160_20002054.name: protocol_fwup_xtea_key_word0
mcu_g_0160_20002054.description: First four bytes (word 0) of the 16-byte XTEA key used by mcu_xtea_decrypt_with_key for firmware data blocks. The reset routine mcu_state_reset_load_key16 loads it from a built-in constant; the contents are deliberately not recorded here, so read that function if needed. Each time the transfer offset passes a multiple of 1 KiB, the handler adds the byte index to every key byte, so the key changes during a transfer. Treat this object as key material. Words 1 to 3 are in protocol_fwup_xtea_key_words_1_3.

mcu_g_0160_20002058.name: protocol_fwup_xtea_key_words_1_3
mcu_g_0160_20002058.description: Words 1 to 3 (bytes 4 to 15) of the same 16-byte XTEA key as protocol_fwup_xtea_key_word0, written only by the reset routine mcu_state_reset_load_key16 and stepped by the 1 KiB key update. The key material is deliberately not recorded here. In builds 12b, 143 and 152 the same logical buffer is described by crypto_auth_key_words_1_3, so this is probably the same key as that authentication key.
